correctness.rationale: Derive [x,y]=beta(x)alpha(y)e1 and prove endomorphism dichotomy P(e1) in ke1. If nonzero, idempotence forces P(e1)=e1, P(e2)=e2+v, P|W=B, B^2=B, Bv=0, giving q^(m-r) I_m(r) at rank r+2. If zero, the image is abelian and lies in H1 or H2 because two linear functionals have vanishing outer product. Projections into H1, H2 and intersection W give q^(2k)I_m(k), I_(m+1)(k) and q^k I_m(k), with inclusion-exclusion. Gaussian-binomial estimates yield 2J_(m+1)(1+O(q^(-m/2))); parity-dependent summable theta tails prove the leading constant and discrete-Gaussian rank law. Independent brute-force enumeration over q=2,3,5 in dimension two, q=2,3 in dimension three, q=2 in dimension four passes, with all bracket/idempotence/rank conditions checked; asymptotics rest on proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The rank-one non-Lie Leibniz family is known, and ordinary q-Gaussian projection counts and their theta limit are known separately. The assessed claim is their structurally constrained full idempotent-endomorphism rank formula and two-hyperplane asymptotic, not the familiar structural classification or ordinary projections. Inspection of the primary full text finds automorphisms, derivations, biderivations and racks rather than idempotent endomorphism rank counts. The relevant centroid-idempotent paper counts a strictly different class; rank counts for semigroup ideals in independence algebras concern the generation invariant, not this cardinality. Repeated mathematical-record and literature searches gave no equivalent or stronger implication. Publication priority is provisional because a general theorem on bilinear-rank-one endomorphism retracts could subsume the formula.

value.rationale: Image ranks of idempotent algebra endomorphisms classify retract dimensions and measure internal splitting structures in a canonical nonnilpotent Leibniz family. The formula gives every rank for every finite field and dimension. The non-obvious asymptotic two-hyperplane law says that almost every retract is abelian and selects one of two algebraically distinguished maximal abelian hyperplanes with asymptotic probability one half each; the parity-dependent rank law adds precise finite-field fluctuations. Neither the classical object classification nor ordinary linear-projection counts alone yield these conclusions.
